claim: William Rodriguez was a maintenance worker at the World Trade Center's North Tower who held a master key to the stairwells and was decorated for heroism after using it to help evacuate survivors on September 11, 2001. He met with the 9/11 Commission behind closed doors, and his account does not appear in the final report. Rodriguez maintains that he felt a powerful explosion or rumble from the sub-basement at 8:46 a.m. which he places seconds before — not after — the aircraft's impact far above, and that a co-worker, Felipe David, reached the basement with severe burns. The mainstream explanation attributes the basement fire and damage to the jet-fuel fireball that descended the building's elevator shafts from the impact zone — an account consistent with Rodriguez's own description of 'the ball of fire [that] went down ... the elevator shaft.' The pre-impact timing, and the controlled-demolition reading it is used to support, are contested and not borne out by the NIST investigation or the official timeline.

notes: Group A on the verifiable core (Rodriguez's role, the master key, the heroism awards, the closed-door Commission meeting, and the absence of his account from the final report — all documented). Group B on the contested core (a sub-basement explosion preceding the impact, used to argue pre-planted charges). The record deliberately surfaces the both-sides hinge: Rodriguez's own account of a fireball descending the elevator shaft matches the mainstream mechanism for basement damage (jet fuel from the impact traveling down the shafts), which undercuts the pre-impact-demolition reading. The reel says the report is '576 pages'; the 9/11 Commission Report body runs 567 pages — minor garble, not material. 'One of five pastries' in the transcript is a whisper mishearing of 'master keys.' Parked on the existing y2001-attack anchor with the other 9/11 cards.
